summary: This excerpt from Kate Douglas Wiggin's novel (labeled Book 11, part 76) covers the Simpson family's move back to their hometown, during which church items were swapped for a bicycle, and Rebecca's growth spurt and the death of baby Mira. Rebecca returns to Sunnybrook Farm for a fortnight, where she finds her household gloomy and Hannah seemingly grown older than aunt Jane.
one_line: A fiction excerpt in which the Simpsons move away amid church-item swapping, Rebecca grows rapidly, and she mourns baby Mira's death at Sunnybrook Farm.
key_facts: Mr. Simpson returned in time to move his wife and children back to the town that had given them birth.
A pulpit chair, several kerosene lamps, and a small stove disappeared from the church during the Simpsons' move.
A village along Abner Simpson's route acquired a magnificent lamp for its new church parlors in exchange for an old bicycle.
Mr. Simpson rode away on the bicycle and was not seen or heard of again for many a long day.
Rebecca shot up like a young tree in the year she began growing, after not growing an inch since age ten.
Miss Jane spent months lengthening skirts, sleeves, and waists to accommodate Rebecca's growth.
Rebecca's dresses were sent to Sunnybrook Farm to be made over for Jenny.
Mira, the baby of the Randall family, died and was buried under a willow tree at Sunnybrook Farm.
Rebecca went home for a fortnight's visit after Mira's death.
Rebecca had been Mira's special charge since Mira's birth.
The absence of John, who had been Rebecca's special comrade, contributed to her sad homecoming.
The pinching economies within the little house depressed Rebecca, who was sensitive to beauty and harmony.
Hannah seemed to have grown into a woman during Rebecca's absence.
Hannah appeared older, soberer, and more settled than aunt Jane.
The narrator observes that it is sometimes the mystery of death that brings one to a consciousness of the still greater mystery of life.
